** *
 NIDHI GUPTA, J.
CM-5100-CII-2023 Prayer in this application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act read with Section 151 CPC is for condonation of delay of 184 days in filing the accompanying appeal.

2. Heard.
3.

For the reasons mentioned in the application which is duly supported by an affidavit of the applicant/appellant No.1, the same is allowed and delay of 184 days in filing the accompanying appeal is condoned.

(O&M) The present appeal has been filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.15,88,750/- awarded by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sangrur (hereinafter referred to as "the learned Tribunal") vide Award dated 02.04.2022 passed in MACP Case No. 66 dated 12.03.2020 filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, (hereinafter referred to as "the Act").
The 5 claimants are 41-year-old widow; 3 minor children; and 58-year-old mother of the deceased Jagdeep Singh, who was about 40 years old at the time of accident.

2. Brief facts of the case are that the learned Tribunal on the basis of pleadings and evidence adduced before it concluded that the deceased-Jagdeep Singh had died due to the injuries suffered by him in a motor vehicular accident that took place on 14.02.2020 due to the rash and negligent driving of a Car bearing registration No.PB-11BN-6655 (hereinafter "the offending vehicle") being Jasbir Kaur And Ors vs Kulvir Singh And Ors on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91581298/
1 driven by respondent No.1; owned by respondent No.2; and insured by respondent No.3.

sentences.text: The learned Tribunal awarded the above said compensation along with interest @ 7.5% per annum.
All the respondents were held liable to pay the said compensation jointly and severally.
3. Learned counsel for the appellants seeks enhancement of compensation by submitting that the income of the deceased has been taken on the lower side as only Rs.9,000/-p.m.
It is submitted that it was the clear case of the appellants that the deceased was doing work of making gates and grills and was earning Rs.15,000/- p.m. to Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Thus, income of the deceased deserves to be enhanced.
Learned counsel further submits that only spousal consortium has been awarded to claimant No.1; and nothing has been awarded by way of consortium to the remaining 4 claimants.
He accordingly prays that the present Appeal be allowed; and the awarded compensation be enhanced in the above terms.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 opposes submissions made on behalf of the appellants and submits that the impugned Award suffers from no infirmity as the compensation awarded to the appellants is just and fair.
Hence, the present Appeal deserves to be dismissed.
5. No other argument is raised on behalf of the parties.
I have heard ld. counsel and perused the case file in detail.
6. It is submitted on behalf of the appellants that the deceased was doing work of making gates and grills and was earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
However, besides a bald statement of the claimants, no documentary evidence to this effect was produced by the appellants.
No customer for whom the deceased may have made gates and grills, was examined by the appellants to prove their case.
As such, learned Tribunal had correctly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.9,000/- p.m. as that of a casual labourer.
Further, Age of the deceased was proved to be 40 years on the basis of his Postmortem Report Ex.C3.
The Tribunal made an addition of 25% towards future prospects.
As there were 5 claimants, learned Tribunal had correctly made deduction of 1/4th towards personal expenses.
Keeping in view the age of the deceased, the Tribunal had correctly applied multiplier of 15.
However, the Tribunal has failed to award any filial and parental consortium to the remaining 4 claimants being 3 minor children and mother of the deceased.

In view of the same, present appeal is partly allowed; and compensation awarded to the appellants is modified as follows: -
